To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strength training adaptations to heavy strength training were attenuated when the strength training was combined with a high volume of concurrent endurance training in well-trained cyclists.
12 weeks heavy strength training with a large volume (90 min per session) of endurance training attenuates the strength training response in well-trained endurance runners.
the strength training adaptations to a 12-week period of strength training are attenuated by a large volume of concurrent endurance training in well-trained cyclists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of high volume of endurance exercise on the strength training response in trained athletes.
the interaction between endurance and strength training and how this interaction can be used to improve performance in well-trained endurance sports.
the effect of concurrent endurance training on the response to heavy strength training in endurance athletes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of strength and power training on muscle strength, hypertrophy, and power is reduced in endurance athletes during a preparatory period of high volume of endurance cycling.
the strength training adaptations are attenuated in well trained endurance athletes during a preparatory period with high volume endurance training.
a large amount of endurance training attenuates the strength training response, which is in line with the previous literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high volume of concurrent endurance training impairs the strength training adaptations in well-trained endurance cyclists.
a large volume of concurrent endurance training impairs strength training adaptations in well-trained endurance cyclists.
a large volume of concurrent endurance training impairs the adaptations in strength and power performance following 12 weeks strength training in well trained endurance athletes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
strength training adaptations are impaired in well-trained endurance cyclists when combined with a large amount of concurrent endurance training.
endurance athletes who wish to improve their muscle strength should consider performing strength training without concurrent endurance training.
strength training adaptations can be improved in endurance athletes during a preparatory period by reducing the volume of concurrent endurance training.
